scenario: [LGRA.8.5.10] / [LTHE.4.1]: both `then` layouts are valid, and a `where` after a step's `within` is that step's, so a one-line sequence's trailing `where` belongs to its last step and there is no sequence-wide `where`. The one-line `A a then B b within 5_s where b.v > a.v` and the same sequence written line-leading must therefore emit the SAME artefact. Drives `dsc_equivalent`: both sources are compiled through to the `.dsc` and compared with the source-position tier dropped, the one thing two layouts may differ in. PATH PINNED: `dsc.parse`'s one-line sequence attaching its trailing `where` with `set_last_step_where`, the helper the `then` line uses, so `dsc.rete` lowers it as the step's join test. A compiler that reads the one-line `where` as the sequence's does not lower it.
rules_ds:
schema A scope ttl 1_h:
    v: Int
    ts: Time

schema B scope ttl 1_h:
    v: Int
    ts: Time

rule r:
    A a then B b within 5_s where b.v > a.v
->
    log info "{b.v}"

expect.equivalent_ds:
schema A scope ttl 1_h:
    v: Int
    ts: Time

schema B scope ttl 1_h:
    v: Int
    ts: Time

rule r:
    A a
    then B b within 5_s where b.v > a.v
->
    log info "{b.v}"
